title: The first accumulation point of scl in free groups is 3/4
body:
## The conjecture

The smallest accumulation point of the set of scl values in a free group is 3/4.

It is approached from below by a one-parameter family with a single twist
parameter. With x = a and y = b a b^{-1} (conjugate, which is what makes these
words homologically trivial),

    w_n = x^n y x^{1-n} y^{-2} = a^n (b a b^{-1}) a^{-(n-1)} (b a^{-2} b^{-1})

of length 2n + 6, and

    scl(w_n) = 3/4 - 1/(2n).

## What supports it

The formula was verified exactly for n = 2, ..., 18. Below 3/4 the computed
spectrum is sparse and thins out sharply going down: of the twenty-five values in
[1/2, 3/4) found by an exhaustive search to length 20, only five lie below 0.65 and
only one below 0.58.

Every infinite family found in the bottom of the spectrum converges to 3/4, and
this one approaches it most slowly, with deficit 1/(2n) at length 2n + 6. A second
family accounts for the two apparent outliers 3/5 and 19/30, and also increases
to 3/4:

    v_m = x^m y x^{-(m-1)} y x y^{-2} x^{-1} y^{-1},
    scl(v_m) = (3m^2 - 3m + 1) / (2m(2m-1)) = 3/4 - (3m-2)/(4m(2m-1)).

That scl(w_n) is a linear-fractional function of the twist parameter is what the
surgery picture of *scl, sails and surgery* predicts, and 3/4 should be the
corresponding surgery limit. That is probably the route to a proof: it would give
both bounds for all n at once and identify 3/4 intrinsically, rather than
certificate by certificate.

The numbers here come from a computation carried out in an AI agent session in
August 2026 using `scallop`, in its rigorous exact-rational mode, and spot-checked
against two independent algorithms. **No person has checked it.** Treat it as
computational evidence and not as established fact.

A search of the literature did not turn up this statement, but that is a weak
negative and should be confirmed by somebody who knows the area.
